newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso hits highest level since Jan. 18.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso hits highest level since Jan. 18.

text.p: The dollar fell a further four pesos against the Colombian peso to close at 1,015, its slowest level since Jan. 18.
The oil and coffee sector sectors, together with some foreign investors, continued to pump greenbacks into the market, dealers said.
"The fall of the dollar is unstoppable and the Central Bank still hasn't stepped in to stop it," one interbank dealer said.
The Central Bank's floating exchange rate band has a floor of 974.73 pesos and a ceiling of 1,121.46 pesos.

The dollar reached an intraday trading low of 1,011 pesos, which later rose as some dealers moved to snap up cheap greenbacks. Dealers reported 335 trades for a total of $125.4 million. The peso opened at 1,017.5 per dollar and reached an intraday high of 1,017.5 pesos, averaging a rate of 1,014.55 over the session.
